notes:
Top-line: Lumina QueryBridge builds an in-app agent for mid-market SaaS customers; interest is narrowly focused on RAG for ticket deflection + fast support agent responses. They need a hybrid retrieval+rerank architecture that stays within tight per-query cost and latency SLOs.

Recent timeline / activity:
- 2026-02-05 discovery call (Jordan, Maya) — overview of Redwood product lanes; Lumina shared telemetry and current stack.
- 2026-02-12 technical deep dive with Lumina infra and search team (Maya, Maya note: heavy emphasis on index size). Fireflies: fireflies:call-20260212-qd8f3.
- 2026-02-20 provided sample trace (12h production traffic) and topology doc; Lumina asked for a replayable load test.
- 2026-03-02 security questionnaire submitted; SEC ticket created (SEC-4911).
- 2026-03-08 pricing sync — they asked for a pricing model keyed to cost-per-qa (embedding + rerank).

Customer technical requirements (copied from notes and call):
- Workload: conversational support agent + background ticket deflection (embed-based recall -> cross-encoder rerank for top-5).
- Index scale: currently ~45M ticket/chunked passages (60B tokens total). Expect growth to ~120M in 12 months.
- Latency SLO (p99): rerank end-to-end for top-5 <= 200ms total; retrieval (ANN) target ~30-50ms, reranker ~120-150ms.
- Throughput target: baseline 100 qps, burst to 300 qps; POC to demonstrate 200 qps sustained.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per query (embedding + rerank) < $0.01; willing to trade some top-k recall for lower unit cost if top-5 precision stays >= 92%.
- Model preferences: open to using Redwood-verified embedding model (dense) and a 7B cross-encoder for reranking; prefer quantized options for rerank if latency improves.
- Routing/fallback: primary in-region dedicated pool, fallback to cheaper multi-tenant hosted variant for non-critical queries.
- Caching: aggressive prefix + hot-query caching expected; want recommendations from Redwood Optimize.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO/SAML and enterprise KMS.
- Audit logs and 12-month access logs retention required for SOC2/audit.
- Data residency: primary US region, but some EU-customer data must remain in EU; need region-aware routing.
- Air-gapped not required today, but roadmap item.

POC scope and success criteria (agreed on 2026-03-08):
- Deploy a Dedicated VPC-based environment with a 2-week replay of 12h production trace at 200 qps.
- Measure p50/p90/p99 latencies for retrieval + rerank, plus cost per query.
- Run golden prompts/QA set to verify top-5 rerank precision >= 92% (measured against current production baseline).
- Deliver recommended batching, quantization profiles, and a cost/latency tradeoff matrix.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't get top-5 to 92% and stay under 200ms p99, we can't replace our current flow." — Head of Search, Lumina.
- "We want predictable spend — show us committed qps pricing vs burst pricing." — VP of Ops.

Existing stack + pain points:
- Annoying: current ANN provider has high tail latencies during reindex windows and the current cross-encoder is hosted on CPU with 300-600ms p99.
- They lack unified observability per-request (token-level cost breakouts) and want Redwood Console features.

- Lumina infra to provide replay credentials and expanded trace (48h sample) by 2026-03-12 (owner: Lumina infra).

Blockers (current):

- EU data-residency mapping needs detailed policy.
